stories.title: Rates are exerting a tightening impulse; transmission to credit and volatility is unresolved
stories.whatChanged: Front‑end and real yields are elevated and modelled term premium is near 0.66%, while canonical credit OAS moves over 20 sessions are small.
stories.whyItMatters: If higher yields push IG/HY spreads and volatility higher, financing costs and equity breadth could deteriorate beyond narrow leadership.
stories.mechanism: Higher policy path expectations and real yields raise nominal rates; that increases borrowing costs and can widen credit spreads if spreads reprice or dealer balance‑sheet capacity tightens.
stories.conclusion: Rates are currently tightening conditions but canonical credit and volatility evidence do not yet confirm broad transmission.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Persistent, multi‑session IG/HY OAS widening plus a canonical MOVE/VIX rise or clear auction tails/dealer selling would confirm transmission.

stories.title: AI/semiconductor leadership is narrow and some issuers show capex‑driven FCF pressure
stories.whatChanged: Semiconductor relative returns lagged Nasdaq (SMH−vs‑QQQ −9.26pp over 20 sessions) and Amazon SEC‑derived simple cash FCF is deeply negative for Q3 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: If capex is pressuring free cash flow at major issuers, durable AI capex depends on operating cash conversion or external financing that could be sensitive to rates.
stories.mechanism: Front‑loaded AI infrastructure spending raises cash PP&E and can push simple FCF negative; sustained negative FCF would require financing or reduced capex guidance.
stories.conclusion: AI/semiconductor leadership remains narrow; issuer filings show capex can materially pressure simple FCF but AI‑specific demand durability is unresolved.
stories.whatWouldChangeMind: Issuer guidance reducing capex, supplier order cancellations for GPUs/HBM, or sustained recovery in AI‑basket breadth would alter the view.

investigations.question: Is recent yield repricing transmitting into IG credit, volatility and broader market stress beyond HY?
investigations.whyItMatters: Determines whether rising yields materially tighten financial conditions and impair credit/funding-sensitive assets.
investigations.currentExplanation: Elevated front‑end and 10Y real yields and an ACM term‑premium uptick are present, but canonical MOVE/VIX and persistent IG/HY widening are missing, so transmission remains unresolved.
investigations.expectedReaction: Conventional: rising real yields/front end should widen credit spreads, lift VIX and weaken broad breadth/small caps.
competingExplanations: Rates repricing is concentrated and has not reached credit/remains limited to duration effects.
Dealer/auction metrics are absorbing supply so far, delaying spread widening.

candidateExplanations.explanation: Concentrated rates sensitivity without broad credit stress.
candidateExplanations.discriminatingTest: Canonical MOVE/VIX uptick and persistent IG OAS widening over next 20 sessions.

candidateExplanations.explanation: Dealer funding and auction demand are temporarily absorbing selling, delaying spread widening.
candidateExplanations.discriminatingTest: Evidence of dealer net selling, auction tails or rising primary dealer participation over subsequent auctions.

investigations.researchNext: Ingest canonical MOVE and VIX series, collect intraday UST/fed‑funds bars, and monitor IG/HY OAS persistence across next 20 sessions. Confirm global duration with Bund, gilt and JGB long ends; cross-check gold versus real yields and USD; review available credit and breadth as context

investigations.invalidationCondition: No persistent IG/HY widening despite sustained long‑end real yield increases.

verified.title: Long-end Treasury stress
verified.detail: On 24 September 2026, the U.S. Treasury par yield curve closed with the 10-year yield at 5.18% and the 30-year yield at 5.47%, confirming severe long-duration rate pressure.

verified.title: S&P concentration remains extreme
verified.detail: Nvidia and Apple together accounted for more than 15% of the S&P 500, reinforcing the concentration risk behind an index that can remain firm even when participation is weaker.

verified.title: Saudi/Houthi energy risk persists
verified.detail: Saudi-led coalition forces said six Houthi ballistic missiles were intercepted on 24 September, with Yanbu among the targeted areas; the report also described claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.

verified.title: Duration stress is global
verified.detail: A Bloomberg global sovereign-bond yield gauge approached 4%, the highest level since 2007, supporting the view that duration pressure is global rather than solely a U.S. Treasury story.

verified.title: Natural-gas storage tightened
verified.detail: EIA reported Lower-48 working gas at 3,351 Bcf for the week ended 18 September 2026, a 53 Bcf weekly injection and 95 Bcf above the five-year average.

verified.title: NBIS analyst catalyst verified
verified.detail: BNP Paribas upgraded Nebius Group from Neutral to Outperform and raised its price target from $260 to $399 on 24 September 2026, independently confirming a catalyst cited in the StockedUp transcript.

verified.title: US–China tariff cliff pushed out
verified.detail: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China agreed to extend their trade truce through 10 January 2027, reducing the immediate tariff-cliff risk while broader negotiations continue.

verified.title: US–Iran diplomacy is active
verified.detail: President Trump said U.S.-Iran talks were continuing during the UN General Assembly and that he believed a settlement would be reached; this verifies active diplomacy but not the transcript's specific Hormuz-for-sanctions terms.

verified.title: Diesel export-policy risk
verified.detail: The U.S. Chamber warned that restricting U.S. diesel or fuel exports could squeeze refiners and risk reducing supplies of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, potentially worsening consumer costs.

verified.title: Late-September midterm seasonality
verified.detail: Citadel Securities' historical midterm-year path shows equities tending to weaken into around September 30 before a stronger average year-end phase; this supports late-September seasonality as context, not a forecast.

verified.title: META Muse catalyst verified
verified.detail: Meta launched its Muse personal AI agent and said it planned integration with smart glasses, independently confirming the product catalyst behind the creator's META discussion.

verified.title: RKLB defence-space catalyst verified
verified.detail: Rocket Lab said it was selected for the U.S. Space Force NITE-STAR IDIQ program, which has a ceiling of up to $981 million across participating vendors, confirming the defence-space catalyst cited by StockedUp.
